title: Building Effective Voice Agents — Toki Sherbakov + Anoop Kotha, OpenAI
talk_summary: OpenAI solution architects describe voice-agent architecture trade-offs (chained STT→LLM→TTS vs speech-to-speech real-time API) and patterns for prompting, tool delegation, evals, and guardrails.

takeaways.technique: Frontline cheap model with tool-call delegation to stronger models
takeaways.what_they_do: A small/fast model handles the common interaction and only calls out via tool to a smarter, more expensive model for hard subtasks, instead of routing everything to the big model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: using like a much smaller model04 mini uh and delegating to that because we don't want uh a smaller model

takeaways.technique: Keep per-agent tool count small; split agents instead of overloading
takeaways.what_they_do: They advise starting each agent with few tools and adding more only as needed, delegating different tasks to separate agents rather than giving one agent 10-20 tools.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't need to connect 10 tools or like 20 tools to a given model. Uh keep the number of tool calls pretty limited

takeaways.what_they_do: They claim the most effective eval step is having humans label real data and iterate prompts from it, before moving to LLM-judge/transcription-based evals with rubrics.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the most important thing is actually havememes to label these data um and actually go and iterate on prompts from there

takeaways.technique: Synthetic conversations between agent and persona clients
takeaways.what_they_do: Run two clients against each other — the agent under test and scripted customer personas — to mass-generate conversations, then extract evals from transcripts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: maybe you have two real-time clients going back and forth across to each other ... simulate like many many of those conversations

takeaways.what_they_do: Run safety/guardrail checks asynchronously on generated text while audio is still being spoken, batching every N characters, exploiting the latency gap between text and output.
takeaways.evidence_quote: run them async uh generally because the generated text from the real-time API is much faster than the spoken audio
takeaways.numbers: guardrail runs every 100 characters in their snippet

takeaways.what_they_do: When handing off between agents, summarize the conversation state and pass the summary so context isn't lost or bloated.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a good pattern to do is actually summarizing the conversation state and then passing it to the other agents so you don't lose any of the the context
